sections.kicker: Prepared for Michelle Kalif by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Michelle asks her clients to stand apart. Her own front door has not done it yet.
sections.keep: The red and black positioning posts. They read as a studio style in one glance.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.

pins.quote: Cuido da forma como a sua marca se comunica, se apresenta e é percebida.
pins.what: The bio describes the service, not who it is for or what is different.
pins.why: Every branding studio cares for how a brand is perceived. The bio does not say why Michelle.
pins.how: Name the client you do your best work for and the one thing you change in their brand.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Prospects hear the same sentence from every designer on their feed.

pins.quote: Querer uma marca mais reconhecida não combina com ser igual à de todo mundo
pins.what: She writes that a recognizable brand should not look like everyone else's. Her grid changes look from tile to tile.
pins.why: Maroon, blue, cream and black, posters and travel photographs. The studio asks for a look and does not show one.
pins.how: Choose two colors and one layout for the posts that carry the studio's voice, and keep life photos in highlights.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: A visitor sees a person with taste and has to guess what the studio looks like.

pins.quote: o que todo mundo deixou de fazer, mas ainda faria diferença para o seu cliente
pins.what: Her best idea is a question about her market: recover what everyone stopped doing.
pins.why: It is a point of view only she has written, and it lives in one post, not in the studio's position.
pins.how: Make this the studio's stance and give the method a name.
pins.label: Your caption
pins.cost: A strong idea stays a post instead of becoming the reason to hire her.
